input.title: The Shape Museum: Vault of Five Doors
input.designRationale: The contract requires five fixed-order items measuring flat/curved discrimination, face-shape identification, the sphere special case, and face-set reasoning, with zero teaching, zero feedback, and zero answer exposure before completion. The core design problem is making a no-feedback experience feel purposeful to a nine-year-old who has evidenced appetite for hard problems and skepticism about faulty logic (reina:riddles:harder, reina:riddles:logic). The solution: a Shape Museum where the child is the newly hired Night Inspector who must file five inspection reports to open the sealed Vault. Filing a report is inherently commitment-based — museums accept reports without arguing back — which makes the absence of correctness feedback diegetic and honest rather than withheld. Each submitted report visibly stamps and slides into a slot beside one of five vault doors; the world reacts to the ACT of committing (stamp, door mechanism turning), never to correctness. Evidence of the child valuing difficulty and questioning logic informed tone (she is treated as a professional inspector, not a student) but was not used to invent a preference: no riddle mechanic, no hint content, no examples were added, because the contract's hintPolicy forbids them. The small-sample feedback favoring color and clear visuals is honored through high-contrast solid renders with the queried face highlighted in a single saturated accent color, exactly as the instrumentHypothesis directs. A visible non-teaching 'Ask the Curator' button satisfies the hintRequested measurement key: pressing it restates only the response format ('Tap one card, then press FILE REPORT'), never geometry content, and the press is logged. Skips are diegetic ('File as Unresolved') so declining never feels like failure and never traps the child. All exposure identities, orientations, option lists, and scoring rules are rendered verbatim from the contract; the design layer adds only framing, pacing, and dignity.
independentlyChosenPrinciples: Commitment before revelation: every world reaction responds to the act of filing, never to correctness, so the no-feedback rule reads as world logic instead of withheld information.

The construct is the only hard thing: all controls are large tap targets (min 96px), no typing, no dragging, no timing, no reading beyond contract prompt text, so response mode never becomes the measured skill.
Dignity by role: the child is cast as a competent professional whose reports are trusted; skipping is a legitimate professional action ('Unresolved'), not a defeat state.

Diegetic instrumentation: hint requests, skips, option changes, and latency are captured through in-world actions the child would take anyway, keeping measurement invisible and evidence uncontaminated.
Honest payoff: the vault opens on completion (all five items terminal), not on score, so the reward never leaks correctness and never punishes wrong answers.
One screen, one decision: each item is a single full-screen scene with prompt, contract-verbatim pictures, and option cards; nothing else competes for attention on the 1365×768 viewport.
Fresh eyes per door: no solid image, highlight, or option from one item ever remains visible during another, protecting the contract's doesNotRevealAnswersTo guarantees.
input.openingPromise: A short animated title card: "The Shape Museum needs a Night Inspector. Five vault doors are sealed. Only your five inspection reports can open them. Nobody has seen what's inside." One large glowing button: "START INSPECTION." The promise is concrete, immediate, and mysterious — file five reports, open the vault — and requires no reading beyond two sentences.
input.firstThreeSeconds: Second 0–1: dim museum hall fades in; five brass vault doors glint in a row; a lantern glow follows an inspector badge that slides to the child with her title on it. Second 1–2: the first door pulses softly and a pedestal rises in front of it carrying the I1 exhibit (cylinder, sphere, rectangular prism, cone, upright standard views, clearly lit and color-separated). Second 2–3: the prompt appears in large type with four big answer cards fanning out below it, and the pulsing outline settles on the cards — visually saying "your move." No tutorial, no narration required; the first tap target is unmistakable.
input.firstAction: Tap one of four large labeled answer cards ("the cylinder," "the sphere," "the rectangular prism," "the cone") beneath the I1 exhibit, then tap the large "FILE REPORT" stamp button that activates once a card is selected. Selecting a card highlights it; re-tapping another card changes the selection (each change logged as optionChangeCount). Nothing is committed until FILE REPORT is pressed.
input.mission: As the museum's Night Inspector, examine five exhibits of solid figures and file one inspection report per exhibit describing their surfaces and faces. When all five reports are filed (or marked Unresolved), the vault's five-lock mechanism releases and the sealed vault opens, revealing the museum's hidden centerpiece. The mission is completion of honest reports, not correctness — the child is told the museum "trusts your judgment and files every report exactly as you write it."
input.coreInteraction: Each of the five doors presents one contract item as an exhibit scene: contract-verbatim prompt (under 25 words, large type, optionally read aloud via a tap-to-listen speaker icon so reading is never the barrier), the exact solids/orientation/highlight specified by the item's exposureIdentity, and the exact option list as large tap cards. Single-select items (I1, I2, I4): tap one card, FILE REPORT. Multi-select items (I3, I5): cards toggle on/off with visible checkmarks; the selectionRule is shown in plain words ("Pick every true statement — there can be more than one"); I5 enforces the contract rule that 'none of them' deselects all others and vice versa, with a gentle wobble animation explaining the exclusivity without teaching content. Every item screen also offers 'Ask the Curator' (logs hintRequested; returns only format restatement) and 'File as Unresolved' (logs noResponse skip). After FILE REPORT, the report card stamps, slides into the door's slot, one lock wheel turns, and the next exhibit rises. The interaction loop is: observe exhibit → decide → select → commit → advance. Independent response always precedes any support, and no support with geometric content exists anywhere in the experience.
input.mathAsPower: The child's geometric judgment is literally the key mechanism: each report is a claim about flat faces, curved surfaces, and face composition, and only a filed claim turns a lock wheel. Deciding whether a sphere has any flat face (C1/C3), naming the circle atop the cylinder (C2), asserting the cone's coexisting flat face and curved surface (C1), and composing the pyramid's full face set against its triangle silhouette (C4) are the only actions that move the world forward. No other verb exists in the experience — you cannot fight, collect, or dodge your way to the vault; you can only reason about surfaces and commit. The causal chain is: mathematical judgment → filed report → lock turns → world advances → vault opens.
input.responseAffordances: All responses are large tap cards (minimum 96×96px hit area, generous spacing) usable by touch or mouse with no precision demand, no drag, no typing, no keyboard, no scrolling within an item. Text is large (minimum 24px) with a tap-to-listen audio read-aloud on the prompt and on each option card so reading skill is not the construct. Selection is two-stage (select, then FILE REPORT) so accidental taps never commit; changing selection before filing is free and logged, never penalized. Multi-select cards show explicit checkmarks and a live count ("2 statements picked") so the child can see the format state. Color highlighting of the queried face (I2's top face) uses a saturated accent plus a hatched texture ring so color-vision differences don't gate the item. Nothing about the interface must be discovered: every actionable element pulses once when the screen loads, and the Curator button restates format on request.
input.stakesAndConsequences: Stakes are narrative and forward-moving: each filed report permanently turns one of five lock wheels, and the vault cannot open until all five doors have a filed or Unresolved report. Reports are final once stamped — the museum "archives every report the moment it's stamped" — which makes commitment meaningful and protects evidence integrity (no revisiting, no answer-shopping). Consequences never touch correctness: a wrong report turns its lock wheel exactly like a right one, an Unresolved report turns it with a grey seal instead of a wax seal, and the vault opens either way. What's at stake is the child's professional act of judgment and the mystery behind the vault, not a score, a grade, or an approval signal. Dignity is preserved because the world treats every committed judgment as valid inspector work.
input.recovery: No state traps the child. Uncertain: 'File as Unresolved' is always visible, phrased as legitimate inspector procedure, logged as noResponse (contract: not scored incorrect), and advances to the next door. Interface confusion: 'Ask the Curator' restates navigation/format only (contract-permitted non-teaching clarification) and is logged as hintRequested; the item is scored as-is per hintPolicy. Accidental tap: two-stage commit means a stray tap only changes selection, never files. Multi-select exclusivity (I5): choosing 'none of them' while others are selected triggers a wobble and auto-clears with a one-line format note, preventing an invalid-state trap. Wanting to stop: an always-available 'End Shift' door in the corner lets the child exit after any item; remaining items log as notAdministered, and the exit scene thanks the Inspector for the reports filed with no vault-denied shaming (the vault simply "waits for the next shift"). Nothing ever loops the child back to a failed state, demands a retry, or blocks progress on a wrong answer.
input.progression: A persistent but unobtrusive strip along the top shows the five vault doors; each terminal item stamps a seal on its door (wax seal for filed, grey seal for Unresolved) and turns its lock wheel with a satisfying mechanical rotation. Items run in the fixed contract order I1→I5, each as a fresh scene with prior exhibits fully removed. Between items a two-second transit beat (lantern glide down the hall) provides pacing without content. The fifth stamp triggers the five wheels spinning in sequence and the vault unlocking. Progression is purely completion-based and visibly one-directional, so the child always knows how far she is and what remains.
input.worldReaction: Every reaction responds to commitment, never correctness. On FILE REPORT: the card stamps with a thunk, ink-press animation, slides into the door slot, and the lock wheel turns — identical animation for correct and incorrect responses. On selection change before filing: the card highlight moves with a soft click, no judgment. On Unresolved: a calm grey seal, the Curator's silhouette nods ("Every honest report helps the museum"), lock turns. On a hint request: the Curator lamp brightens and the format restatement appears in a speech card, then dims. On I5's invalid combination: a physical wobble and format-only note. On completion: all five wheels spin regardless of score and the vault opens. No sound, color, animation timing, or character expression differs by answer correctness anywhere, eliminating side-channel answer leakage.
input.payoff: When the fifth report reaches terminal state, the five lock wheels spin in sequence, the vault doors part with rolling fog and warm light, and the hidden centerpiece is revealed: a slowly rotating, luminous 'Impossible Gallery' — a kinetic sculpture of all the museum's solids orbiting a light source, casting shifting silhouette shadows on the vault walls (a purely aesthetic spectacle; it displays no face labels, no answers, and no item content, so it cannot contaminate the contract's evidenceRequiredNext follow-ups). The Inspector's badge is embossed with a vault emblem and a factual shift summary appears in-world: "Reports filed: N. Unresolved: M. Curator consulted: K times." — attempts, assistance, and completion stated as museum records, with no stars, no score, no mastery language.
input.replayVariation: Replay does not re-administer the five contract items: their exposure identities are single-use evaluation evidence, and repeating them would contaminate independence and enable memorization. Instead, a returning Inspector finds the vault already open and is offered 'Gallery Patrol' — a free-exploration mode of the opened vault sculpture with cosmetic variation (lantern colors, hall weather through the skylight, badge polish) and no measurement, no geometry questions, and no answer exposure. Any future measured content comes only from a separately contracted follow-up evaluation (per evidenceRequiredNext), presented as a 'new wing' of the museum with fresh items; this design deliberately builds no self-generated replay items.
input.visualDirection: Warm nocturnal museum palette: deep teal-charcoal hall, brass and copper door hardware, amber lantern light. Exhibit solids are the visual heroes: matte, softly shaded 3D renders in distinct saturated hues (honoring the child-feedback preference for visible color) on neutral pedestals against a dark backdrop for maximum figure-ground contrast. The queried surface (I2 top face) gets a saturated accent fill plus a hatched outline ring for color-vision safety. Perspective is a consistent three-quarter view matching each item's exposureIdentity, with the cylinder top drawn as an honest ellipse (a contract-acknowledged confound, not hidden). Typography: large rounded humanist sans, max ~25 words per prompt per the instrumentHypothesis, high contrast cream-on-dark. Option cards are cream parchment 'report lines' with generous padding. UI chrome is minimal: door-progress strip on top, Curator and Unresolved buttons anchored bottom corners, nothing else.
input.motionDirection: Motion is calm, mechanical, and commitment-flavored: lantern-glow eases (400–600ms cubic ease-out) between scenes, pedestals rise with a soft settle, cards fan out with 60ms stagger. The FILE REPORT stamp is the signature motion — a decisive 200ms press with a 1-frame squash and paper slide into the door slot — identical for every answer. Lock wheels rotate 72° per filed report with weighted deceleration. Nothing during deliberation moves or loops (no idle bouncing near options) so latencyMs reflects thinking, not distraction. Selection highlight is an instant border glow, no travel animation, keeping optionChangeCount cheap and honest. All motion is skippable-fast (<700ms) so pacing never inflates latency measures; a reduced-motion mode swaps animations for crossfades.
input.soundDirection: Sparse and diegetic: low ambient museum room tone, faint clock tick in transit beats, soft paper rustle on card selection, a satisfying rubber-stamp thunk plus lock-wheel ratchet on FILE REPORT — the same sounds for every answer, correct or not, guaranteeing no audio correctness leakage. Curator interactions use a warm two-note lamp chime. Unresolved filing uses the identical stamp thunk with a slightly softer seal press, dignified rather than sad. Prompt and option read-aloud uses a clear, neutral recorded voice triggered only by the speaker icon (never autoplay, so it doesn't pace or pressure). Vault opening earns the only musical moment: a rising warm brass-and-glass swell. Master mute is one tap and persistent.
usefulLibraries: React (scene/state management for the five-item fixed-order flow and terminal-state completion rule)
Zustand or XState (explicit item state machine: presented → selecting → committed/skipped, guaranteeing no re-entry into committed items)
react-three-fiber + three.js (consistent, orientation-accurate 3D solid renders per exposureIdentity, plus the vault payoff sculpture)
Framer Motion (stamp, lock-wheel, and transition animations with prefers-reduced-motion support)
Howler.js (identical-per-outcome commitment audio, tap-to-listen prompt narration, persistent mute)
date-fns or native performance.now wrapper (precise latencyMs from item render to commit, per measurement keys)
anticipatedChildConfusions: I1: she may read 'flat' as 'thin/lying down' (contract confound) — mitigated only by clean upright renders and read-aloud, never by defining 'flat', which the contract forbids.

I2: the perspective ellipse may block the 'circle' label — the render keeps an honest but gently foreshortened top; the confound is logged as a possible interpretation, not patched with a top-down cheat view that would alter exposure identity.

I3/I5 multi-select: she may believe only one card can be true (contract confound) — the on-screen selectionRule text 'there can be more than one' and the live selection count address format, not content; under-selection is recorded as partialCreditPattern/underSelectionCount per contract.
I5 exclusivity: combining 'none of them' with another card — prevented by the auto-clear wobble with a format-only explanation.

Expecting rightness feedback after filing (she questions logic and may probe): the opening narration pre-frames it — 'the museum files reports without judging them; the archive is opened later' — making silence coherent.

Expecting a content hint from the Curator (evidence shows she requests hints when stuck): the Curator's first line on any press states 'I can only explain how to file, not what to write' — a format boundary set in-world, with the press still logged as hintRequested.
Fearing a wrong report blocks the vault: the intro states all five wheels turn on filing, and the door strip visibly confirms it after item 1.
instrumentRisks: Elimination without understanding: I1 admits success by spotting the one curved-only option (contract confound); latencyMs and optionChangeCount are captured to support the contract's guessing-estimation follow-up but the instrument cannot resolve it alone.

Carryover: cylinder appears in I1/I2 before I5; per contract, I5 is reported as conditional evidence for C3, and the design removes all prior exhibits from view to minimize visual (not memory) carryover.

Multi-select format burden (I3/I5) may masquerade as misunderstanding; the design lowers burden (checkmarks, count, plain selectionRule) but the format-burden control remains an evidenceRequiredNext item, not something this instrument claims to solve.

Narrative pressure: the vault mystery could push fast guessing over careful reasoning; mitigated by no timer, no urgency music, static deliberation screens, and the Inspector framing that valorizes careful reports.
Read-aloud voice inflection could inadvertently cue an option; recordings use flat, uniform prosody across all options and are reviewed for cue leakage.
Ellipse rendering of the cylinder top (contract-acknowledged) may cause a circle-vs-ellipse labeling failure that is representational, not conceptual; flagged in output as a possible confound on I2.
The dignified Unresolved path could invite over-skipping; skip rate is reported factually and the intro frames filing a best judgment as the inspector's normal duty without penalizing skips.
input.engagementPrediction: Prediction: given evidence of appetite for difficulty and sustained engagement with hard multi-step problems (reina:riddles:harder, reina:riddles:scaffold), a nine-year-old cast as a trusted professional will complete all five items in one sitting (estimated 4–8 minutes), with zero or one End Shift consideration, at most one or two Curator presses (likely on the first multi-select), and deliberate latencies (5–30s per item) rather than sub-2s guessing. She is predicted to reach the vault payoff and voluntarily linger in it briefly. This prediction is an engagement hypothesis only and, per the contract, is never treated as evidence about her geometric understanding.
falsifyingEvidence: Exit via End Shift before item 3 falsifies the prediction that the inspector framing sustains a full five-item sitting.
Median per-item latency under ~2 seconds with high correct-by-chance plausibility falsifies the claim that the world induces deliberate reasoning rather than tap-through.
Three or more Curator presses, or repeated presses on the same item, falsifies the claim that the first required action and formats are understandable from the finished screen.
Two or more Unresolved filings on single-select items falsifies the claim that commitment feels safe and dignified rather than risky.
High optionChangeCount (>4) combined with long stalls on multi-select items falsifies the claim that the response mode is not itself a burden being measured.
Declining or ignoring the vault payoff after completion falsifies the claim that the payoff is earned and motivating.

Any observed behavior suggesting she believes the stamp sound or lock turn signals correctness falsifies the claim that world reactions are correctness-neutral, and would require an audio/animation audit.
input.measurementResponsibilities: Per item, capture exactly the contract's measurement keys: I1/I2/I4 → selectedOption, correct, latencyMs (item-render to FILE REPORT), optionChangeCount, hintRequested; I3 → selectedOptionSet, exactSetCorrect, partialCreditPattern, latencyMs, optionChangeCount, hintRequested; I5 → selectedOptionSet, exactSetCorrect, overSelectionCount, underSelectionCount, sphereSelected, latencyMs, optionChangeCount, hintRequested. Additionally log per item: noResponse (Unresolved), notAdministered (End Shift early exit), read-aloud usage (reading-support exposure), and I5 exclusivity-wobble triggers (format friction). Report factually: attempts per item, assistance events (Curator presses, all format-only), exposure record (which solids/orientations were shown, confirming freshness contracts), possible confounds observed (fast latencies suggesting elimination, under-selection patterns, ellipse-related hesitation on I2, cylinder carryover into I5 marked conditional per contract), friction events (wobbles, repeated Curator presses), and completion state per completionRule (responded/skipped/notAdministered per item). Output per-construct status limited to provisional-support, provisional-gap, or indeterminate; never declare mastery, never mark a construct established from this single sample, never report a learning-style or preference claim, and flag I5's C3 evidence as conditional when I2 was answered correctly, exactly as the contract requires.
